A birth scene that made a generation rethink what survival truly means.

Even though it was a box office success, Mel Gibson believes the film could have done much better if Disney hadn’t pulled it from theaters so quickly. Speaking on The Joe Rogan Experience, Gibson explained that Apocalypto faced tough competition during its opening weekend.

“Apocalypto had no stars, it was in another language, and it opened the same weekend as a film with Leonardo DiCaprio and another with Cameron Diaz,” Gibson said. “All three came out at the same time, and the one with no stars and a different language actually won the weekend financially—by a narrow margin.”

According to Gibson, the surprise win didn’t translate into a longer run.

“In the second week, Disney pulled the screens,” he added. “I thought that was funny because Apocalypto was another self-funded project. So maybe the distribution deal wasn’t as good as the others. But you know—it’s a business.”

source_details.synopsis: Apocalypto () is a 2006 epic historical action-adventure film produced and directed by Mel Gibson, who co-wrote the screenplay with Farhad Safinia. The film features a cast of Indigenous and Mexican actors consisting of Rudy Youngblood, Raoul Trujillo, Mayra Sérbulo, Dalia Hernández, Gerardo Taracena, Jonathan Brewer, Rodolfo Palacios, Bernardo Ruiz Juarez, Ammel Rodrigo Mendoza, Ricardo Diaz Mendoza, and Israel Contreras. Set in either Yucatán or Guatemala during the year 1502, Apocalypto portrays the hero's journey of a young man named Jaguar Paw, a late Mesoamerican hunter and his fellow tribesmen who are captured by an invading force.
